reason: The cited evidence (E1) directly supports the first four premises with experimental and simulation data on the same material and mechanisms. The fifth premise—that a homogenization treatment can reduce local compositional fluctuations—is a standard metallurgical concept but is not specifically demonstrated or cited for this alloy system, representing a minor gap.
premises: CoCrFeNi HEA nanopillars exhibit ultrahigh uniform tensile ductility (~110%) at high flow stress (0.6–1.0 GPa)
This ductility arises from spatial and synergistic coordination of deformation twinning and dislocation slip
The twinning–slip coordination is enabled by atomic-level chemical compositional heterogeneities
These heterogeneities produce wide variations in generalized stacking fault energy and dislocation activities
Homogenization heat treatment can reduce these local compositional fluctuations and stacking fault energy variations
